physical_mismatches.reason: Laminar flow assumption stated in methodology (Section 2.1, page 6) but Realizable k-ε turbulence model applied (Table 2, page 3); flow regime not clearly specified at Re based on inlet velocity 0.1 m/s and characteristic length
No transient analysis; steady-state only. Real microelectronic thermal management involves transient startup, power cycling, and thermal time constants not captured
No thermal feedback control or dynamic power management. Chip power fixed at constant 8 W without temperature-dependent throttling or adaptive control
Single-phase air cooling only; no phase change, liquid cooling, or enhanced cooling modalities discussed as potential extensions
No reliability analysis (thermal cycling, solder joint fatigue, material degradation over time)

studio_assumptions: Steady-state thermal and fluid flow conditions
Air as ideal gas with constant properties (density, viscosity, specific heat, thermal conductivity)
No radiation heat transfer; only convection and conduction modeled
No-slip boundary condition at all solid walls
Heat source generates constant uniform heat flux boundary condition at chip-substrate interface
Aluminum fins and heat sink base with constant material properties (k, ρ, Cp)
Turbulence modeled via Realizable k-ε with standard wall functions
Pressure outlet condition maintains overall flow rate while allowing exit pressure variation
Hexahedral mesh with mesh-independence validated at 265,075 to 414,765 cells depending on fin type
